root_cause: The public language switcher and static localized-route builder treated both locales as prefixed. That made English to Dutch navigate to /nl/* and caused Dutch canonical, hreflang and internal-link generation to diverge from the agreed public authority where Dutch is unprefixed and English lives under /en/*.
prevention: Dutch public routes are always canonical and unprefixed.
English public routes are always canonical under /en/*.
Runtime language switching must preserve path, query and hash while mapping NL→EN to /en/* and EN→NL to the unprefixed route.
Static localized-route generation must use the same canonical mapping for internal links, canonical URLs, hreflang and og:url.
Legacy /nl and /nl/* URLs permanently redirect to the matching unprefixed Dutch route.
Production browser proof must execute a real NL→EN→NL roundtrip and fail if the Dutch return path contains /nl.
